A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSync and contain readable main text, equations, four tables, nine figures, and Appendices A-G. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HDTF and AIGC-LipSync evaluations, a 39-participant user study, component ablations, and qualitative appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative evaluations, user-study outcomes, ablations, and qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2, Eq. (2), replaces the stated noise-prediction loss with conditional flow-matching velocity regression. This is a localized revision of the reported objective: both versions already claim Flow Matching, and the architecture, sampling strategy, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish retraining.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MEAD and 400 hours of YouTube data and evaluate on HDTF and the same 615-video AIGC-LipSync benchmark. Appendix E retains the same subject categories and challenging visual scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain Wav2Lip, VideoReTalking, TalkLip, IP-LAP, Diff2Lip, MuseTalk, and LatentSync. Appendix Figure 5 retains EchoMimic, Hallo3, and Sonic; the other qualitative comparator sets also match. The added SyncTalk++ citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, generation-success assessment, training budget, and inference settings are unchanged. Both versions report 80,000 training steps, sampling threshold 850, initialization parameter 0.92, and 50 denoising steps. The user study retains 39 participants, 32 video sets, and five-point ratings.

E4.justification: Table 4 and Figure 4 retain the same sampling, initialization, and CFG ablations. The appendix comparisons, lip-shape-leakage examples, and video-description ablation in Figures 5-7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same user-study reliability statistic, Cronbach's alpha of 0.98. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-4 and the qualitative examples remain unchanged. For example, OmniSync's HDTF FID remains 7.855, and its AIGC generation-success rates remain 97.40% overall and 87.78% for stylized characters. No result entries or findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Beyond replacing Eq. (2), v2 defines the conditional velocity target as (Vab - xt)/(1 - t) and specifies the interpolation path xt = (1 - t)x0 + tVab. This revises the mathematical training specification; the remaining equations are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning universal mask-free synchronization, progressive noise initialization, dynamic spatiotemporal guidance, and the first AIGC-LipSync benchmark. Their claimed performance advantages and applicability are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of pose preservation, lip-shape leakage, guidance tradeoffs, and text conditioning remain unchanged in the main text and appendices. Appendix F retains the same misuse discussion and deployment qualifications; no substantive limitation is added.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including AdamW, learning rate 1e-5, batch size 64, 64 A100 GPUs, 80-hour training, and Whisper/T5 conditioning. Appendices A and E retain their training and benchmark-construction details, and the project link is identical.

R1.justification: v2 adds SyncTalk++ as reference 29 and cites it alongside SyncTalk in the introduction's discussion of pose and identity limitations. The other works and substantive research positioning are retained; subsequent reference-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 revises the short explanation surrounding Eq. (2), updates the affiliation and internship wording to Kling Team, and replaces the preprint notice with NeurIPS 2025 conference information. The section order and nearly all remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised equation and explanation alter spacing and text flow around the existing tables and figures, moving the conclusion's start from page 9 to page 10. All nine figures and four tables retain their organization and visual content; there is no substantial display redesign.

improvement.justification: The explicit velocity-matching objective and target in Eq. (2) better document the Flow Matching training already claimed in v1. This is a limited gain: the new interpolation path remains unreconciled with the retained denoising-time and noise-prediction notation, while the empirical evidence and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged.
